name: Acamar
text: Acamar’s floating drydocks survived the relay collapse by keeping every hull welcome. Its desalination guild exports water; Mara’s relief office occupies an old customs booth.

name: Adahn
text: Adahn was settled around a deep aquifer that is slowly failing. The dust refineries still run, but freighter water keeps the reservoir settlements alive.

name: Aldea
text: Aldea’s seed vault fed the first stranded ships. Its orchard communes still vote on crop shares beneath the glass roof of the original lander.

name: Andevian
text: Andevian grew from a salvage yard into the Compact’s precision foundry. Ore goes into its pressure domes; machines and finished hulls come out.

name: Antedi
text: Antedi’s cloud cities began as refinery platforms. Its factories need imported ore, and technicians are always in short supply, which makes automation especially valuable.

name: Balosnee
text: Balosnee’s ring stations sheltered displaced theatre companies. Their recordings travel farther than their ships, and crews on long isolated runs are always hungry for new diversions.

name: Baratas
text: Baratas keeps medicinal greenhouses beneath its ice. The clinic served both sides of the relay strikes, and its scattered outposts depend on it whenever fever spreads.

name: Brax
text: Brax is the last relay station still answering distress calls by name. Its volunteer survey crews chart safe routes, using machines repaired well beyond their intended lives.

name: Bretel
text: Bretel’s amber skies hide salt flats and heat collectors. A water-ration ledger became its first constitution, and the port council has never quite stopped arguing about it.

name: Calondia
text: Calondia’s cooperative granaries once guaranteed the outer stations a harvest. Blights come and go in the wet fields, and when a crop fails, imported food bridges the gap.

name: Campor
text: Campor’s miners bought their own landing field after the old concession company withdrew. Ore is plentiful; replacement machinery arrives aboard independent ships.

name: Capelle
text: Capelle’s ring foundries supply security outfits across the Reach. Rival crews contest the same mining belt, so ore and weapons are always in demand.

name: Carzon
text: Carzon’s wildlife preserves support a tightly licensed fur trade. Ranger families police the seasons, while station merchants insist their own inventories are endangered.

name: Castor
text: Castor’s storm observatories share their orbital habitats with musicians. The Cooperative’s public navigation forecasts are assembled here between exceptionally long concerts.

name: Cestus
text: Cestus is a bare rock with no native life, wrapped in sealed habitat tunnels. Its old heating plant fails in most cold seasons, which makes warm clothing a practical luxury.

name: Cheron
text: Cheron’s ice cutters supply the agricultural moons. They lack modern foundries, so ore must be imported even as tankers leave heavy with melted ice.

name: Courteney
text: Courteney is the frontier’s last dependable repair stop. Settlers rebuilt its cracked cisterns from ship plating; water and dependable components remain welcome cargo.

name: Daled
text: Daled’s first colonists planted beneath thin ice and called it a garden. The soil is poor and the grow lamps are patched, so a failed crop leaves families dependent on food ships.

name: Damast
text: Damast’s iron claims are worked by family crews. The Freehold charter forbids selling the landing field, after a company once tried to invoice the town for its own runway.

name: Davlos
text: Davlos’s ring labs study unusual fungi used in both medicine and prohibited stimulants. Customs law changes at the border; traders must read the local manifest rules.

name: Deneb
text: Deneb’s remote robot foundry was meant to build the next generation of relays. The collapse stranded its specialists, and labor is always scarce, so every production run is a negotiation.

name: Deneva
text: Deneva’s terraced farms share their surplus through a rotating council. The old beacon never went dark, and its light is still a promise of food to arriving crews.

name: Devidia
text: Devidia’s herb gardens grow inside cooled canyons. Its clinics are thinly staffed, so when an outbreak comes, harvests alone cannot replace finished medicines.

name: Draylon
text: Draylon’s gas-skimming stations mark the surveyed frontier. Nothing lives on the giant itself, so every habitat is sealed, and each carries a memorial to a missing ship, and pilots trade stories of relays still waiting beyond the dark.
